caveats: All roots, excludes and evidence paths are relative to repoRoot. Evidence uses the form file:line.

skillshub contains no vendored whisper.cpp or other C/C++ headers. `git ls-files skillshub` lists no .h/.c/.cpp files. The vendored native code is elsewhere: desktop/src-tauri/vendor/vosk (libvosk.dylib, vosk_api.h), magios/Vendor/vosk, and magesp/components (a Waveshare BSP plus a patched FT5x06 touch driver, magesp/main/idf_component.yml:3-14).

The docs disagree on the remote-Linux shape. docs/components/scripts/container-runtime.md:165-171 says a container on a separate Linux host 'needs a paired, authenticated outbound desktop session ... explicit host file access ... Not implemented'. docs/ARCHITECTURE_V2.md:240-266 and desktop/src-tauri/src/edge_client.rs say the Magician Edge outbound session exists for CUA, browser.cdp and iMessage. The likely reading is that Edge capabilities are done but explicit host file grants are still pending.
Kindle has no network code yet. Its transport design is marked DESIGN ONLY (docs/plans/2026-08-28-kindle-client-auth-and-transport-design.md:3-4).

The Dockerfile copies only magician, magicutor and magic-supervisor into the image (Dockerfile:50-56). decision-engine (supervisor-managed when installed, magic-supervisor/src/main.rs:102) and the macOS Swift helpers are therefore native-only.

setups.name: Magican installs native services on the Mac
setups.summary: This is the product path for a single Mac, and what make install, the setup wizard and the desktop app's Install native services here all set up. From a source checkout, one shared installer builds Magician, installs a checked package under ~/.magician, seeds the data root without overwriting anything, registers the supervisor as the per-user LaunchAgent ai.magicbeans.magican.backend, and waits until Magician, Magicutor, Pi, the memory model and the desktop gateway are ready. Desktop can also install a prebuilt checksummed package, and on later launches it makes sure the service is started. Desktop-managed native Magician listens on the LAN by default so phones can use the Same Wi-Fi route. This option is enabled only on macOS; the code also has a systemd user unit and a Windows logon task, but the option is shown as disabled on Linux and Windows.

placement.installed software: Mac, ~/.magician (MAGICIAN_PREFIX), kept apart from the data
placement.ollama: Mac, native (the memory embedder stays resident)

setups.desktopRole: Installer and lifecycle owner of the native backend (launchctl), plus the host gateway, which also reports permission grants to terminal setup, and all native surfaces.
setupCommands: Desktop: Install native services here (MAGICIAN_SOURCE_DIR selects the checkout)

setups.name: Everything native on one Mac (developer stack)
setups.summary: The foreground developer flow: `make run-all` runs every piece natively from your terminal. magic-supervisor runs natively on the Mac and supervises magician (:3002) and magicutor (:3003). Vite serves the unified UI on :5173, proxied to :3002. The debug desktop tray binds the host gateway on 127.0.0.1:3017 before the supervisor starts, so provider discovery can reach it. Ollama runs natively on :11434 and :11435. `make run-all` also starts the persistent Cloudflare tunnel and the code-graph server. On macOS, `make install` now installs the native login service instead (the next setup), so stop that service before running this flow.

placement.decision-engine: Mac, native, supervisor-managed when the binary is installed
placement.channel bots: Mac, daemons spawned by the runtime

setups.desktopRole: Host-side companion. It provides the 3017 gateway (screen capture, AppleScript, AX/CUA relay, speech, reminders, iMessage), plus the tray, Orb, HUD, voice wake and Settings. It does not own the backend lifecycle in this flow.
setupCommands: launchctl bootout gui/$(id -u)/ai.magicbeans.magican.backend (stop the installed service first)

setups.name: Backend in a Linux container on the Mac
setups.summary: magician, magicutor and magic-supervisor run in the debian-slim OCI image. On macOS 26+ Apple Silicon this uses Apple's container runtime; otherwise it uses Docker or Colima. Host services stay native: Ollama, the desktop tray and gateway, and Chrome. The host data root is bind-mounted as /data, and the image serves the built UI from /app/ui on :3002. There are two owners. (a) The composed installer (FLOW=container) publishes 3002 and 3003 and sets MAGICIAN_HOST_GATEWAY_URL to host.docker.internal:3017 or host.container.internal:3017. It also stops host-native magicutor so the extension dials the container's :3003. (b) The Desktop option 'Install and manage a local container' publishes 13002->3002 and 13003->3003, and reaches the native gateway through a private exec-pipe relay rather than host-alias forwarding. A third variant, 'Connect to a local container', has Desktop attach to an existing loopback container without owning its lifecycle.

placement.magic-supervisor / magician / magicutor: Linux container on the Mac (Apple Container VM or Docker/Colima VM)
placement.chrome extension: Mac Chrome, dialing the container's published :3003
placement.decision-engine / macOS Swift helpers: not in the image (Dockerfile copies only three binaries)

setups.desktopRole: Optionally owns the container lifecycle (runtime detection, image pull, credential custody, /data seeding, health checks every 5 s). It always remains the native capability host on :3017.

setups.name: Server in a container on a Linux box
setups.summary: Linux runs the stack through the container flow; a native Linux install is still manual. Docker runs the image with --network host, so the container shares host loopback and Ollama is at 127.0.0.1. The install is headless. The macOS tray phase is skipped, and Mac-only skills are hidden by the host_gateway availability gate. Durable pairing keys live in a gnome-keyring Secret Service inside the image. The Linux desktop AppImage can optionally manage the local Docker backend and act as this computer's CUA/browser edge.

placement.desktop app: optional Linux AppImage on the same host (manages local Docker), otherwise none

setups.desktopRole: None required. A Linux Desktop can manage local Docker and act as the edge. Mac-only capabilities are unavailable.

setups.name: Remote Linux engine with the Mac Desktop as Magician Edge
setups.summary: Canonical chat, task, memory and workspace data stay on a remote Linux engine (container) reached over HTTPS. The Mac Desktop chooses 'Connect to a remote container'. It enrolls through the server's authenticated Settings page using a one-time magican://connect Desktop Edge link, and stores a desktop-only credential in the OS keychain. It then dials outward over WSS to /api/magician/v2/edge/bridge. Over that session it advertises host.cua (installed driver tools), browser.cdp (while a loopback Magicutor reports a connected extension) and read-only host.imessage/query (macOS only). The server invokes these through POST /api/magician/v2/edge/devices/{id}/invoke under generation-fenced, short-lived grants. The public server never routes inbound traffic to the loopback :3017 gateway. Phones, ESP32 and the UI address the remote engine directly. Desktop skips local container supervision for a remote origin.

paths.say: The desktop app dials out to the remote server over a secure websocket, with Cloudflare Access headers when the server sits behind Access. Nothing listens on the Mac.

paths.via: Edge invoke frames on the same socket
paths.say: Over that same socket, the server borrows the Mac's screen control, browser and read-only iMessage, and only what the desktop offered.

paths.via: HTTPS REST plus wss realtime (TLS required for non-loopback)
paths.say: The desktop's own windows talk to the remote server over HTTPS and a secure websocket; anything off this machine must use TLS.

paths.via: connect.<zone> /api routed to the remote URL, or the remote origin directly
paths.say: Phones keep using connect dot your domain, now routed to the remote server, or they talk to the server directly.

setups.desktopRole: Edge proxy for machine-local capabilities: CUA, browser/CDP via local Magicutor and extension, and iMessage. It does not supervise any backend and rejects engine-owned local file access.
setupCommands: Desktop: Change setup -> Connect to a remote container -> open Desktop Edge link

setups.name: Phone and device access through connect.<zone> (Cloudflare Tunnel plus Access) or Same Wi-Fi
setups.summary: iOS, Android and ESP32 learn one stable protected origin at enrollment: connect.<zone> (MAGICIAN_CONNECT_HOST). A named Cloudflare tunnel path-splits that host. /host/* goes to this desktop's gateway on :3017. /health and /api/* (REST and WebSockets) go to the explicitly selected backend: native :3002, container :13002, or a verified remote HTTPS URL. Switching backends never changes the hostname and needs no re-enrollment. Cloudflare Access requires a shared service token plus a revocable per-device Magician token. Only the one-time enrollment exchange path bypasses Access, guarded by a five-minute single-use capability. The alternative, Same Wi-Fi, uses the server-advertised private LAN address.

placement.cloudflared: the desktop machine, brew service or token connector
placement.selected backend: native Mac, local container, or remote server

paths.say: Phones and the ESP32 call connect dot your domain. Behind Cloudflare Access, its API paths go to whichever backend you chose, and each request also carries the device's own key.
Host paths on the same address go to this Mac's desktop app, so phone requests for the Mac's own tools run here.

paths.via: private LAN address advertised by the server
paths.say: On the same Wi-Fi, a phone can skip the tunnel and use the private address the server advertises.

setups.desktopRole: Owns route selection (Settings -> Network) and keeps /host/* on the desktop. It issues the enrollment QR codes. Android App Pilot uses a separate Desktop-issued QR.

setups.name: Public webhook and dev-UI ingress (single named tunnel)
setups.summary: An opt-in persistent named Cloudflare tunnel (MAGICIAN_ENABLE_FUNNEL=1) runs as a brew service in browser-login mode or as a token connector. It maps webhook.<zone> to the Kapso receiver on :3010, which forwards to magician :3002. This host must never be behind Access, because providers cannot log in. ui.<zone> maps to :5173 and should be behind Access; HTTPS is needed for mic and voice on phones. Notes open at /notes in the authenticated app and need no separate notes hostname. The tunnel stays up across stop-all.

paths.say: WhatsApp messages arrive from Kapso at the public webhook address, which stays outside Access, and the bot checks each one's signature before passing it to Magician.
The developer UI gets its own address behind an email login, so a phone browser gets HTTPS for its microphone.

evidence: scripts/ensure-magician-tunnel.sh:172-174 (Notes use the app sign-in; no separate notes ingress)

setups.name: Several Magician machines, one tunnel each
setups.summary: When an owner runs Magician on several Macs (e.g. a MacBook Pro and a Mac Studio), each machine gets its own tunnel magician-<machine> and its own hostnames. This avoids Cloudflare load-balancing requests to the wrong machine. <machine>.<zone> carries /api and /health to :3002 and /host to :3017 behind Access. ui-<machine>.<zone> goes to :5173, and webhook-<machine>.<zone> goes to :3010 and :3011. iOS keeps one connection profile per paired machine.

placement.each Mac: full native stack plus its own cloudflared connector

paths.say: With several Macs, each one has its own tunnel and address, so a phone always reaches the machine it paired with.

setups.desktopRole: Same as the single-Mac setup on each machine.

setups.name: Windows or Linux Desktop with a container or remote engine
setups.summary: The standard non-macOS deployment runs Magician, Magicutor and the supervisor from the Linux OCI image, either locally or remotely. The native Linux AppImage or Windows NSIS Desktop stays on the user's computer as its CUA, browser and platform-tool edge. Linux can manage a local Docker backend or select a remote engine. Windows can manage the image through Docker Desktop, connect to an existing local container, or select a remote engine. Native Windows backend executables and Task Scheduler support are a future path, and Linux and Windows never advertise iMessage.

placement.backend: local Docker (Engine on Linux, Docker Desktop on Windows) or remote server

setups.desktopRole: Container manager and/or Edge for local CUA and browser. No macOS host features.
setupCommands: Desktop setup: Install and manage a local container | Connect to a local container | Connect to a remote container
